What does condo management cost in Washington, DC?

For Washington, DC condo boards · Updated November 14, 2026

The short answer

Published DC-area rate cards run from about $12 a unit a month for accounting only to $35 to $50 a unit for full service, usually with a monthly minimum, and before extras like project oversight, resale certificates and mailings. For a 12 unit building, full service at those rates costs about $5,000 to $7,200 a year before extras.

Typical rates by level of service

What a 12 unit building would pay a year at each level, using published DC-area rates and minimums:

Rates vary by company, building size and what is included. Get two or three written quotes.

The fees on top

The per-unit fee is rarely the whole bill. Ask every company about:

  • Setup or onboarding fees when you start.
  • Project oversight, often a percentage of the project cost, such as 10% of a roof repair.
  • Resale certificate and admin fees, often charged when an owner sells.
  • Mailings, copies and late fee processing, sometimes with a markup on postage.
  • Vendor markups when the company hires its own vendors.
  • Extra meetings, after-hours calls and collections referrals.

What you pay either way

The management fee is only part of your dues. Insurance, utilities, repairs, vendors, reserves, the tax return and any audit cost the same whether or not you hire a manager.

What self-managing costs instead

A self-managed board trades the management fee for its own time, plus software and any help it chooses to buy: a bookkeeper or accountant for the tax return, a lawyer for collections that go to court, and an advisor if the board wants one. The work is the same: meetings, budgets, dues, notices, filings, insurance renewals and records.

Questions to ask in a quote

  1. What is the monthly fee, and is there a minimum?
  2. Which services are included, and what is billed extra?
  3. Do you mark up vendors, postage or supplies?
  4. Whose bank account do dues go into?
  5. How much notice to end the contract, and is there a fee?
  6. What records do we get back, in what format, and how fast?
